answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a ferrous as the anchor of the cost. A orchard stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a cedar...
